tour.name: Chiang Rai Private Day Trip from Chiang Mai: White Temple, Blue Temple & the Golden Triangle

tour.overview:
Three hours north of Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai province reaches the Mekong river, where the borders of Thailand, Laos and Myanmar meet at the Golden Triangle, once the centre of the world's opium trade. In and around the town of Chiang Rai, contemporary Thai artists have created some of the most surprising temples and buildings in the country.

This private day takes you there and back from Chiang Mai with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the White Temple, the life's work of artist Chalermchai Kositpipat, the Blue Temple and the Black House, then drive to the Golden Triangle for lunch and a boat ride on the Mekong.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Chiang Mai
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, long-tail boat
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Mae Kachan hot springs.
• Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple.
• Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Blue Temple.
• Baan Dam, the Black House.
• The Golden Triangle and the Mekong.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private car makes this long day comfortable, with stops when you want them, and we reach the White Temple early, before the coach tours.

WHO IT SUITS
Art and architecture lovers, photographers and anyone with a few days in Chiang Mai.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day, choose our Chiang Mai temples or elephant sanctuary tours; with more time, spend a night in Chiang Rai.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about three hours each way on good mountain roads. Covered shoulders and knees are required at the temples. Visiting Laos or Myanmar requires visas and is not part of this tour.

days.name: Hot springs, the White Temple, the Blue Temple, the Black House, lunch and a Mekong boat at the Golden Triangle
days.description:
What to expect: Chiang Rai's extraordinary modern temples and the Golden Triangle, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets, boat and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at 7:00 for the drive north through the mountains. You stop for coffee at the Mae Kachan hot springs, where steaming water bubbles up beside the road and you can boil eggs in the spring.

At about 10:00 you reach Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple. Since 1997 the artist Chalermchai Kositpipat has been rebuilding this temple at his own expense as a gift to the Buddha, and it will not be finished in his lifetime. Covered in white plaster and pieces of mirrored glass that sparkle in the sun, it represents the purity of the Buddha. To reach it you cross a bridge over a sea of reaching hands, symbols of desire, and inside, the murals mix Buddhist imagery with superheroes, spaceships and scenes of modern life. Nearby, a golden building houses – unusually – the toilets, gold symbolising worldly desire.

You visit Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Blue Temple, finished in 2016 by a student of Chalermchai, its interior an intense sapphire blue around a white Buddha, and Baan Dam, the Black House, a collection of some forty dark wooden buildings filled with horns, skins and bones, created by the artist Thawan Duchanee as a meditation on death. In the afternoon you continue to the Golden Triangle at Sop Ruak, where the Ruak river joins the Mekong between Thailand, Laos and Myanmar. After lunch with a view of the three countries, you board a long-tail boat on the wide brown Mekong. You drive back to Chiang Mai, arriving at about 19:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Chiang Mai.
08:45 – Mae Kachan hot springs.
10:00 – Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple.
11:15 – Wat Rong Suea Ten, the Blue Temple.
12:00 – Baan Dam, the Black House.
13:15 – Lunch at the Golden Triangle.
14:15 – Long-tail boat on the Mekong.
15:15 – Drive back to Chiang Mai.
19:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Hall of Opium museum at the Golden Triangle can be added.
• A night in Chiang Rai allows the Doi Tung royal gardens or a hill-tribe village visit.
• Some long-tail boats stop at a Lao market island; we do not include it, as it requires buying souvenirs to justify the stop.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, temple tickets, Mekong boat, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Hall of Opium, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is it a long day?
faq.answer: About 12 hours, with roughly 6 hours of driving on good mountain roads. A night in Chiang Rai makes it more relaxed.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the White Temple and the Black House, plus the Mekong boat. The Blue Temple is free.

faq.question: Do we enter Laos or Myanmar?
faq.answer: No. You see both countries from the river and the viewpoint; crossing requires visas and is not included.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, with a view of the Mekong. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the sparkling White Temple and the boat. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The temples are on flat ground with some steps; boarding the long-tail boat needs a little agility.

faq.question: What is the dress code?
faq.answer: Cover shoulders and knees at the temples. Wraps can be bought at the entrance.

faq.question: Can we visit a hill-tribe village?
faq.answer: We prefer not to include 'human zoo' villages. With a night in Chiang Rai, we can arrange a responsible community visit.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to February is cool and clear. March and April can be hazy from crop burning.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
